ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, as amended by the Financial Intelligence Centre Amendment Act 1 of 2017 and the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combating Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Companies Act 71 of 2008; Companies Regulations 2011 (including beneficial ownership filing requirements under Regulation 21A and CIPC Form CoR 21.1); Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorist and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004; FIC Directive 6 on prescribed payment limits and accountable institution customer due diligence.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the parent or foreign shareholder (or equivalent registry extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or registrar of the foreign parent jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the issuing jurisdiction is party to the 1961 Hague Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization at a South African Embassy or High Commission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or tax authority of the foreign parent jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address for each proposed director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent authority in the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if required by CIPC or the receiving financial institution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Declaration (CoR 21.1 or equivalent UBO register extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicant company and its directors or beneficiaries
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required for domestic filing; notarization and legalization may be required where the declaration is signed outside South Africa

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders, and counterparties against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the South African domestic terrorist list under the Protection of Constitutional Democracy against Terrorist and Related Activities Act 33 of 2004, the OFAC SDN List and EU/UK consolidated lists where a foreign nexus exists, and the FIC AML/CFT directives. Politically exposed persons as defined in the Financial Intelligence Centre Act must undergo enhanced due diligence, including source-of-funds documentation for trade finance and documentary letters of credit in the copper cathode transaction chain. A risk-based approach under FIC Guidance Note 4 applies, with mandatory reporting of suspicious or unusual transactions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services (Companies and Intellectual Property Commission online name reservation and filing portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be submitted in any of South Africa's 11 official languages using Latin script; non-Latin characters must be transliterated to the Latin alphabet. The name must end with the statutory suffix 'Proprietary Limited' or its approved abbreviation '(Pty) Ltd', or the Afrikaans equivalent '(Edms) Bpk'. The selected name must not be identical to or confusingly similar to an existing registered company name, trademark, or foreign entity protected under the Companies Act 71 of 2008.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If CIPC rejects a name reservation, the applicant may (i) file a new name reservation application through CIPC e-Services, or (ii) where the rejection is based on third-party objection or an adverse similarity finding, apply to the Companies Tribunal under Section 160(2) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 within 15 business days of the rejection notice using Form CTR 142, attaching the CIPC rejection letter and evidence of distinctiveness. Reserved names are non-transferable and automatically lapse if the company is not registered within the 180-day validity period; no extension is permitted by statute. Re-application after lapse may be made on the portal at the then-applicable prescribed fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are permissible provided the registered office remains a physical street address in South Africa at which legal process can be served during business hours and where the company's statutory records are maintained. A P.O. Box or purely digital address is not lawful. For a non-ferrous copper cathode trading company operating via LME warrant transfers and documentary letters of credit, persistent reliance on a virtual office without locally stationed management, physical operational controls, proper trade records, and a South African bank account will fail commercial substance expectations and materially increase AML/CFT risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 30% annualized probability of an unannounced physical inspection for a medium-risk enhanced due diligence entity engaged in base metals trading; the risk increases on any reported suspicious transaction, documentary discrepancy, or CIPC beneficial ownership verification campaign.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended including by the Companies Amendment Acts 16 and 17 of 2024; applicable provisions include ss 13-19 (incorporation and registration), s 15 (Memorandum of Incorporation), s 4 (solvency and liquidity test), s 38-40 (share issues), s 66 (board), and s 76 (directors' duties).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), established under s 185 of the Companies Act; principal office at 77 Meintjies Street, Sunnyside, Pretoria; electronic filings via CIPC e-Services at www.cipc.co.za.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) filed together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (Form CoR 15.1A for a standard private company).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up share capital. The MOI may provide for par-value or no-par-value shares, and any allotment or distribution must satisfy the solvency and liquidity test under s 4. No government escrow account is mandated; escrow arrangements, if any, are contractual requirements imposed by the commercial bank rather than by statute.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: 1. The company be incorporated as a private company under the name [PROPOSED NAME] (Pty) Ltd, and that the Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation be approved for submission to the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission. 2. The registered office be established at [PHYSICAL ADDRESS], South Africa, with effect from the date of incorporation. 3. The incorporators' subscription of [NUMBER] ordinary shares in the stated proportions be accepted, consideration being satisfied by contribution into the corporate bank account. 4. [NAME] and [NAME] are appointed first directors, each accepting the duties imposed by section 76 of the Companies Act. 5. The directors are authorised to register the company for all taxes, open bank accounts, and execute all ancillary documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services portal; Companies and Intellectual Property Commission, Pretoria
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log on to the CIPC e-Services platform and run a pre-registration name search against the companies register using up to four proposed names in priority order under Regulation 12. If the preferred name is available, lodge Form CoR 9.1 (Reservation of Company Name) electronically and pay the prescribed reservation fee. The reservation is valid for six months and prohibits registration of the same or a confusingly similar name by another applicant. If no proposed name is accepted, incorporate using the company registration number as the provisional name and apply for a name change after registration.
required_dossiers: Certified ID or passport copies of proposed incorporators and directors (certified within three months)
Form CoR 9.1 Reservation of Company Name
List of up to four proposed names in order of preference
Motivation or consent letters if the name includes restricted words (Regulation 14)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC rejects the name as undesirable, confusingly similar, or already reserved, the applicant may file a formal defence with the Companies Tribunal within 10 business days, resubmit Form CoR 9.1 with alternate names, or proceed with a numbered company name and later apply for a name change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC pre-filing validation; preparer: registered law firm or authorised company formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI) using standard Form CoR 15.1A or an approved custom MOI conforming to s 15 of the Companies Act. Complete Form CoR 14.1 (Notice of Incorporation), including the registered office address, the names and consents of the first directors, and the prescribed declaration of compliance. Each incorporator must sign the MOI and the Notice, and the signatures of directors must be witnessed. If any incorporator or director is a foreign resident, their signature must be notarised and apostilled in accordance with the Hague Apostille Convention before submission.
required_dossiers: Draft MOI (CoR 15.1A) signed by each incorporator
Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1) signed by each incorporator
Consent to act as first director (included within CoR 14.1)
Certified ID or passport copies of all incorporators and directors
Proof of physical registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CIPC may issue a pre-registration Notice of Defective Compliance. The preparer must amend the MOI or Notice and resubmit within the period stated in the notice (generally 20 business days). If the defect concerns signatures or consents, obtain fresh witnessed signatures before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CIPC Online Filing, Fee Payment and Registration Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC e-Services / BizReg electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed CoR 14.1 and MOI to the CIPC e-Services portal, complete the online declaration that the incorporation requirements of the Companies Act have been satisfied, and pay the prescribed incorporation fee by EFT or card. CIPC validates the application and, upon approval, issues the enterprise number, the company registration certificate, and the formal registration notice under s 14(1)(a). The company acquires juristic personality on the date and time stated in the certificate of incorporation under s 19(1)(a).
required_dossiers: Certified copies of incorporators' identity documents
Proof of payment of the CIPC incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where CIPC suspends or queries the application under a Notice of Defective Compliance, cure the specific defect and resubmit within the stated period, generally 20 business days. Alternatively, withdraw and re-file the application, preserving the existing name reservation where it remains valid.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); eFiling portal: https://efiling.sars.gov.za; SARS customs division administers import/export controls.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign company must register through SARS eFiling or a SARS branch. Income tax registration requires submission of the IT101 registration form (for non-resident companies, the representative taxpayer in South Africa) together with proof of incorporation, memorandum of incorporation, directors' details, and a physical address or letter of appointment of the local agent. VAT registration requires a separate VAT101/102 application where the foreign entity is conducting an 'enterprise' in South Africa and the value of taxable supplies exceeds the registration threshold. SARS issues an income tax reference number and a VAT vendor number upon successful registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a 'check-the-box' election regime. A Pty Ltd is automatically a taxable person and resident if incorporated or effectively managed in South Africa. Relevant elections include: (i) VAT grouping election under section 50A of the Value-Added Tax Act, allowing two or more companies to be treated as one vendor; (ii) headquarter company election under section 9J of the Income Tax Act; (iii) corporate reorganisation rollover elections under sections 45 and 47, enabling tax-neutral asset-for-share transactions; and (iv) controlled foreign company high-tax exemption election under section 9D(2)(f), where foreign tax paid at or above 75% of the South African headline rate may exempt CFC income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory VAT registration is triggered where taxable supplies exceed ZAR 1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period; voluntary registration is permitted where taxable supplies exceed ZAR 50,000 in any consecutive 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: South Africa does not impose a mandatory real-time electronic fiscal clearance mandate for commercial invoices. A vendor must, however, issue a valid tax invoice containing prescribed particulars under section 20 of the VAT Act before claiming input tax. VAT returns are filed electronically via SARS eFiling. Customs export declarations and manifest clearances are submitted electronically through the SARS Customs clearing system (e.g., e@Cargo and the SASAS/CDS environment). There is no national digital stamping requirement; SARS is progressively modernising towards structured e-invoicing but has not enacted mandatory real-time e-invoice clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act where the goods are supplied to a purchaser outside the Republic and are exported from South Africa within 90 days after the time of supply, provided documentary proof of export is retained. Services are zero-rated under section 11(1)(k) where supplied to a non-resident and the services are physically rendered outside South Africa, or under section 11(1)(l) for services in relation to movable property that is exported/imported, subject to the non-resident not being in South Africa at the time of supply. The supplier must be a registered vendor and must retain prescribed export evidence in order to support a refund claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: SAD500 Customs export declaration (or DA550 re-export declaration) stamped and cleared by SARS Customs
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, or other transport document evidencing physical export from South Africa
Commercial invoice describing the copper cathodes, quantity, price, and terms of sale
Bank statement, SWIFT payment instruction, or inward foreign remittance confirmation evidencing receipt of the export consideration
Packing list and, where required, a certificate of origin or London Metal Exchange warrant transfer documentation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may disallow zero-rating where the vendor does not hold sufficient documentary evidence of export within the VAT Act's prescribed retention period. The consequence is a retrospective VAT clawback of 15% output tax on the consideration, together with interest under section 239 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 and understatement penalties up to 150% of the shortfall for intentional non-disclosure. Deliberate submission of false export documents or claims is a criminal offence carrying imprisonment and additional monetary penalties under the Customs and Excise Act and the Tax Administration Act. Further, failure to comply with exchange-control repatriation deadlines may lead to rigorous anti-money-laundering review and administrative sanctions under the Currency and Exchanges Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through the Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv) and authorised dealers (commercial banks)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Africa maintains a liberalised current account with full convertibility for trade-related payments, while capital account transactions remain subject to SARB exchange control approval via authorised dealers. Dividend and profit remittances by non-residents are permitted without prior SARB approval provided the entity is in good standing with SARS, the remittance is funded from after-tax retained earnings, and an authorised dealer submits the required Form MP337 and supporting documentation (audited financial statements, tax clearance certificate, and resolution). No general capital gains tax (CGT) withholding applies on share sales, but CGT is imposed on the seller. The Financial Surveillance Regulations require that any capital movement not specifically exempted or delegated to authorised dealers must obtain prior approval. Non-resident shareholders may receive dividends subject to dividend tax at 20% unless reduced by a double taxation agreement. In practice, inward-listed entities and qualifying foreign investors enjoy significant fungibility of funds, but outward transfers of capital by residents and any offshore funding guarantees require regulatory reporting. The 2023 amendments to the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Exchange Control Regulations) further aligned the regime with a risk-based authorised dealer framework, reducing pre-approval burdens for low-risk current transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the SARB Currency and Exchanges Manual, all export proceeds from physical goods must be repatriated to South Africa within 180 days from the date of shipment unless an extended dispensation or waiver is granted by an authorised dealer. Exporters must obtain a unique Export Number from their authorised dealer before shipment and declare the transaction through the Form EXP for customs and exchange control purposes. The mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts is zero in highly exceptional circumstances: the dealer may allow retention of foreign currency in an approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA) provided the funds are earmarked for bona fide current account commitments or the exporter's working capital. For a copper cathode wholesale trading entity, the default SARB policy requires full repatriation and conversion into ZAR, but an FCA retention facility may be approved up to the exporter's verified foreign currency expenditure or, if justified, a higher limit with dealer approval. Any FCA balance not used within the approved purpose must be converted on receipt. Complete supporting evidence (bill of lading, commercial invoice, export customs declaration, and proof of receipt) must be retained for five years. Failure to repatriate within 180 days constitutes a contravention of the Exchange Control Regulations and may attract penalties of up to R10,000 per contravention plus potential criminal prosecution.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Standard Bank of South Africa Ltd
Rand Merchant Bank (a division of FirstRand Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Specialised Trade Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium for offshore digital EMIs as primary clearing rails. South African exchange control regulations require that all cross-border trade settlements flow through an authorised dealer in South Africa for reporting and monitoring. Offshore EMIs (e.g., Revolut Business, Wise Business, Payoneer) may be used as ancillary collection or disbursement tools for minor amounts, but they are not recognised as authorised dealers for SARB purposes and cannot issue the required SARB-compliant export documentation (Form EXP, export number generation, or Bill of Entry confirmation). They also create practical obstacles for SARS tax clearance and transfer pricing substance. The entity may, however, maintain an offshore FCA held with a foreign bank if approved by an authorised dealer, and that FCA may be operated through electronic platforms. Onboarding viability of a pure digital EMI is assessed as 'Medium' for non-regulated auxiliary accounts and 'Low' for primary treasury accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is not statutorily mandated for corporate account opening, provided the directors and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) undergo a remote verification process using a Risk Management Approach compliant with the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA) and the 2022 directives. Major South African banks accept remote account opening for a proprietary limited company if the responsible person is a director and the verification is completed via live video conference, biometric checks, and digital notarisation of passport copies. In practice, FNB, Standard Bank, and Absa require at least one director to be physically present at a branch for the first mandate / FATCA / CRS sign-off if the company has no existing relationship with the bank. If all directors are foreign residents, banks may require the in-person appearance of a designated director at a South African branch, or, alternatively, the appointment of an authorised local agent / introducing bank to perform the due diligence. The decision is bank-specific, but the standard compliance posture is: remote opening available for South African-resident directors; foreign-resident directors may trigger a physical interview or a sworn affidavit with apostilled certified copies.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership and lack of SARS tax clearance certificate for the entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed FICA corporate account opening form; Certified and apostilled Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI); Directors' and UBOs' certified passports; SARS registration letter confirming income tax number and VAT registration; Valid SARS tax clearance (Good Standing) certificate issued within 90 days; Bank mandate resolution signed by all directors; Beneficial ownership register filed with CIPC; Notarised proof of physical address (lease or utilities); Business plan and projected cash flows; Source of funds declaration for initial capital; Notarised passports and council tax/bank statements for UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure of counterparties or clients (copper cathode trading with offshore refineries and traders)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Know-Your-Counterparty (KYC) files for all trading partners; Trade contracts and Incoterms; Bills of lading and warehouse warrants (LME-approved wharf storage); Documents against payment / LC terms; Proof of commercial substance (office lease, payroll records, board minutes); Transaction flowcharts; Sanctions screening results (OFAC, EU, UN, South African targeted financial sanctions list); Negative news / adverse media searches for counterparties; Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) questionnaire for politically exposed persons (PEPs), if any.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potentially structuring transactions to avoid reporting thresholds (deposits/cash withdrawals in consolidated ZAR value > R24,999 per transaction or cash aggregations)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cash limit compliance policy; Detailed cash flow projection showing no cash-intensive operations; Bank statements evidencing wire-only settlements; Board resolution mandating electronic funds transfers only; Internal audit trail for all payment chain approvals; Treasury policy prohibiting cash structuring; AML training certificates for finance staff.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of complex ownership or trust/offshore corporate layers that obscure UBO identification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO chain documentation up to natural persons; Group structure chart; Share registers and shareholding certificates; Trust deeds and written trustee confirmations; Register of directors and prescribed officers; Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) Beneficial Ownership Filing; Notarised identification copies of all UBOs; Memorandum explaining economic rationale for any offshore holding companies; Audited financial statements at each holding level.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent document signatures, expired directors' IDs, or foreign-language company records
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original witnessed bank mandate forms; Apostilled or notarised translations (English) of all foreign records; Certified resolutions from foreign parent board appointing South African signatories; Certified copies of MDAs and SOIs; Up-to-date CIPC company extracts and annual returns; Signed declarations by local representative confirming authenticity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant capital injections into South Africa must be routed wire transfers in freely convertible currency to the entity's authorised dealer (commercial bank) with a clear purpose code. Inward transfers by non-resident shareholders are classified as 'Capital Invested' and require completion of the Form BI (Block A and Block D) by the recipient through the authorised dealer. The bank will issue a BI certificate for each inward transfer, which is essential for future repatriation of dividends, shareholder loans, or sales proceeds. The preferred routing is SWIFT MT103/MT202 with a detailed remittance instruction referencing 'Contribution of Share Capital to ZA Pty Ltd' or 'Subscription for Ordinary Shares'. Supporting documentation must include: board resolution of the foreign shareholder, share subscription agreement, updated MOI (if applicable), and the entity's SARS registration. The authorised dealer verifies the source of funds, sanctions checks, and the CMS (JSE/SARB) reference if the transfer is executed through NOSTRO corridors. No SARB pre-approval is required for foreign direct investment (inward share capital, equity or loan funding) as it falls within the authorised dealer dispensation, but the bank must file the appropriate BI form within 30 days. The shareholder loan must be subordinated if it will be treated as soft capital for regulatory purposes; otherwise, it is a capital account transaction requiring loan agreement documentation and interest rate benchmarking. Incoming payments relating to physical copper cathode imports (advance payments, documentary collections, or LC drawdowns) must be classified as 'Current Account' with appropriate trade purpose codes as per the authorised dealer's BOP coding manual.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements must clear through the entity's authorised dealer using either SWIFT MT103 (for direct telegraphic transfers) or a Documentary Letter of Credit (for open-account and LC-backed purchases of copper cathodes from offshore suppliers). All outbound applications must cite the underlying commercial invoice, copy of the bill of lading/airway bill, certificate of weight/quality, and insurance certificate. For a ZA-based importer-trader, the bank will review the transaction for compliance with SARB's 180-day payment rule (for imports, payment must be made within 180 days of shipment unless an approved forward cover or extended terms apply). The entity may use an Import Documentary Letter of Credit (sight or usance) opened with a South African issuing bank; the bank will require a trade finance facility or 100% cash cover if unsecured. SWIFT MT103 from an FCA is permitted if the funds are retained under an approved FCA limit, but most trade settlements will route through a ZAR current account that is converted to USD/EUR/GBP at the bank's ruling rate. For physical copper cathode purchases from DRC/Zambia or other African suppliers, the trader must ensure the payment terms comply with the SADC and SACU customs protocols; the use of a Standby Letter of Credit (SBLC) or Bank Guarantee for key shipments is common. All outbound wires require a 'reason for payment' code that maps to the SARB Balance of Payments Survey; the authorised dealer will debit the client's current account and file the BOP return on the same value date.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward Exchange Contracts (FECs) with authorised dealers for firm delivery of USD/ZAR and cross-currency (EUR/USD, GBP/USD) for trade-receivable and payable exposures

Non-Delivery Forwards (NDFs) on USD/ZAR permitted when the underlying transaction is a genuine trade exposure and the authorised dealer confirms that the client has no natural ability to deliver the currencies
Cross-currency swaps and basis swaps between ZAR and hard currencies for the tenor of a trade finance facility, subject to SARB 'underlying exposure' requirements

Currency options (vanilla put/call) purchased from authorised dealers to hedge copper cathode purchase price and currency risk on LC payables; option writing not authorised without special dispensation
Commodity-linked FX swaps and rolling forwards executed through the JSE's currency derivatives platform or bilateral banks, provided that settlement occurs through an authorised dealer
Foreign Currency Accounts (FCA) as a non-derivative hedging rail allowing retention of export proceeds in USD for up to the FCA approved limit to mitigate short-term conversion risks

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act 2008, s33) for Proprietary Limited Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary date of incorporation; annual filing date is the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts CIPC late penalty; continued default leads to a compliance notice, administrative deregistration after at least 30 days' notice, loss of legal capacity, and potential director liability for debts incurred while trading deregistered.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually with the CIPC Annual Return; within the same 30-business-day anniversary window; updated filings required within 7 business days of any shareholding transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing is treated as non-compliance under the Companies Act; CIPC may issue a compliance notice, and persistent failure may support deregistration; administrative penalties apply under the Companies Amendment and AML/CFT framework.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) including audit report (if public interest score triggers audit)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: CIPC (filed together with the Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after financial year-end; mandatory AFS copy must be submitted to CIPC together with the annual return when audit/review is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to prepare and file is a director offence under Companies Act s30/s33; directors may be liable to a fine and/or imprisonment; CIPC may treat the annual return as incomplete and commence annual-compliance enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months of the financial year-end (or earlier if SARS prescribes an effective date)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit invites SARS administrative penalties of up to 200% of assessed tax for non-disclosure, statutory interest at the prescribed rate, and criminal proceedings for false declarations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Sixth month of the year of assessment for the first provisional payment; last business day of the year of assessment for the second provisional payment; optional top-up within 7 months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Underestimated provisional tax may attract a 20% penalty on the shortfall, plus prescribed interest; non-submission triggers administrative non-compliance penalties and possible criminal sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Companies Act 2008 and Companies Regulations 2011, a mandatory independent audit is triggered if Public Interest Score (PIS) equals or exceeds 100, or if the company's Memorandum of Incorporation, a regulatory requirement, or group consolidation requires it; for the copper-cathode wholesale arbitrage entity, annual turnover commonly exceeding ZAR 100 million places it above the PIS audit threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB and applied under the Companies Act 2008; IFRS for SMEs is available for eligible companies below the PIS audit threshold; no separate Local GAAP alternative applies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, at or before the anniversary annual return filing, the company must file a Beneficial Ownership Declaration with CIPC; any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership must be reported to CIPC within 7 business days of the change, and the register of beneficial ownership must be kept current at the registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Mortgages and Charges over Shares (if any)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 - USD 30,000 per annum for a statutory IFRS audit performed by a registered auditor

stage_6.statutory_headline_rate: 27% for years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023 (28% previously)
stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday; s11D R&D (150% or 50% deduction?), s12B renewable energy, s12BA, s12C machinery allowance, s12L energy efficiency; but note: the effective rate can be reduced by assessed loss carryforwards and allowances.
